I bought this game when it was on sale for 4,99 €. I have already played the very good game "Shadow of Mordor" and read that it was highly inspired by the Batman series, so I thought I should give it a try.
When I started the game I wanted to play it on "hard" mode, but the game mode description (warning! This is super hard and only for very experienced players that know the game very well) made me select normal mode.
After playing a little less than 1 hour of the game, I wanted a refund. Here is what I wrote as my reasons:
"The combat comes in slowmo mode and requires no skill. The controls feel sluggish. The story and acting are almost unbearable. And I think if I play it for a  few more hours I will get claustrophobia from the cramped environment.
I can imagine that this game was awesome and revolutional back at the time where it was released and maybe because the gameplay was new, it had to be made that easy. But it just feels like a waste of time now. Skill wise, I would recommend this game to little children or people completely new to gaming. While it's of course not suited for children (way to dark and brutal), adult newcomers to gaming or unskilled gamers should be able to enjoy this."
Then I remembered that I only played on normal so far and thought it would only be fair to give it another try on hard mode before judging it like this. So I did, and I must say I was not disappointed.
While I don't really like the acting and characters in this game, the story by itself is really not bad. I think it must be awesome for Batman fans.
But the combat on hard mode is really fun and challenging. Almost every fight is good. Especially the special and boss battles are not repetitive, there is always something fresh to each new fight.
The SloMo is a matter of taste, I don't really like it, because it at first messed up my fighting rhythm. But it's ok once you get used to it and can even look cool and make you feel like a badass sometimes.
Oh and about the claustrophobia: I found out that (luckily) the game also features different areas, including out doors, so there is quite some nice variance of scenery in the game.
The puzzles are quite easy, but entertaining and a nice change to the fighting.
So my verdict: I can really recommend this game. But if you are a at least moderately skilled player or even have played similar games before, I highly recommend starting it on hard, because normal mode is babysitting you.

The Touhou Project, a franchise of Doujin Games that I have known since about 2006.  It is well known for it's large cast of characters, music, and lore.
HSiFS is no different in this regards.  Storywise, it has the playable cast investigating why the seasons have been thrown completely out of whack.  The playable cast this time includes Mainstays Reimu and Marisa, and for the first time in a non-spinoff, Aya and Cirno are also playable.  The game's gimmick is the season mechanic.  Each character has a main season they are locked into, and a subseason the player selects to either compliment their main season, or to offset it's weaknesses.  The selected season also contains a secondary 'special/bomb' which turns shots into items.  Personally, I feel this mechanic works well, but can come off a little forced, but it is far superior to Legend of Lunatic Kingdom's absurd difficulty spike.  (The games are hard enough as is)
In all, I am excited Touhou has finally come to steam, and I wish ZUN the best of luck in securing an audience here!

This game is also known as Out Of This World, it follows the story of a professor named Lester who gets transported to an alien planet after a particle accelerator test goes haywire. I still own this game on Sega Genesis and this 20th Anniversary remake is true to its predecessor.
Graphics: 10/10
I love the art-style in this game, it is unique and at the time of release was WAY PAST advanced. It was unique unlike any other game and still is to a large extent. The colors are vibrant and things that you need to notice stick out pretty well. Since you are on an alien planet the drawing and color of it really brings forth that imaginative environment. I recommend playing this on the highest settings it will let you, it looks a lot better than the original game. You can switch settings by pressing Y on your controller or setting it that way so you can see what it was like on Genesis. It makes it pixelated and takes away a lot of the background scribbles that really give the environment more life, I recommend playing on high quality.
Sound: 9/10
I only really noticed the music at the beginning and at the end, the game could have used a little bit of ambiance, but it is no big deal, not many screens are empty and there is 99% of the time always something going on that requires you to either sit back and think and analyze what is going on or, most of the time, requires you to have fast reaction time. Anyway, the sound effects are awesome needless to say, the game in my opinion could have used a little more ambient music but it isn't something you really notice.
Gameplay: 8/10
So, let me be honest. This game is TOUGH. Much like a lot of classic games from back in the day. They are unforgiving and only TRUE WARRIORS OF VIDEO GAMING can overcome it. If you beat this game without using a guide, kudos to you. I did it way back in the day when I was younger, today I needed it for a part that I ALWAYS get stuck at. I use an XBOX controller so keep that in mind as you read the rest of this section. You get your direction buttons, an action or shoot button, and a jump button which is basically your up button. Holding A makes you sprint while you are running or charges your gun. You get 3 gun levels, basic shoot by pressing A, holding it until a little ball appears gives you a shield for a brief time, and holding until a LARGE ball appears gives you a super blast to destroy shields and breakable walls. It isn't a hard game to pick up and play, it IS a hard game to beat however.
Story: 10/10
For what the game is, I think the story is amazing. There is no voice acting, but you do have your alien companion try and communicate with you in a tongue you won't understand. Your character tries to by friendly at first with a raise of his hand in attempts of "hello" but it falls on deaf ears. Without spoiling anything, like I said above, you end up on an alien planet, you have to explore a bit and outrun a beast, then you get imprisoned by the alien inhabitants. The story follows you, Lester, and his attempt to escape from this world. The story very much relies on the alien you befriend toward the beginning so making sure he stays alive is just as important as keeping yourself alive. The puzzles are challenging and you will have a tough time figuring out every little detail to move on, especially toward the middle of the game, but stick with it. This is one of very few games that really make you feel accomplished when you beat it.
Overall: 9/10
I'm debating between an 8 and 9, but I'll give it the 9. It is a unique game that has an original art-style and story that are really entertaining and well done. Like I said, it could use a little ambient music but that is okay, and just beating the game is a big challenge in the first place. If you pick this up, I recommend trying to grab it on sale, it'll be worth the money. At time or writing I think the default price is $10, which isn't bad and is about what the game was worth when it released anyway.
Also I would like to add, this version of the game comes with achievements. Most you will unlock with story progression, one or two of them you'll probably come across anyway but require a tad bit of extra "exploration" (or standing still for 30 seconds *wink wink*).

Without so much as a spoken word, this game encapsulated me and probably helped shape my love of video games since I was a child.  When I played this game in the early 90's, I just thought it was neat.  When I played this game again recently, I was still impressed, even when I removed the rose-tinted glasses of nostalgia.
The mechanics are simple, and although there is little direction given, it is not impossible to determine the course of events that need to occur in order to advance.  Sometimes it does require trial-and-error, but the checkpoints (or chapter breaks) were frequent enough to not be too much of a nuisance compared to other games of the era.
Of course, the presentation is still out of this world (sorry). The storytelling in this game is probably the best example I could give of what got me hooked into having a video game tell a cinematic story.  The story itself may be basic, but the fact that you could show a story that did not rely heavily on dialogue or narration and have a flow that kept interest in the game throughout almost the entire journey blew my mind as a kid, and I was still impressed when I booted it up months ago.
If you haven't already played this game before, I still recommend it. I can't say the same for many of the other games that I have played in the early 90's.

Very bad. I do not recommend this game at all.
There are so many things broken, badly designed or implemented in this game that I don't know what to start with. Actually, it's a waste of time to even address each issue, since there are so many so I won't even do that. This feels more like an attempt to cash in from the fame of the Resident Evil franchise rather than a fully fledged game.
The single player campaign if I may call it like that is a purely laughable mode put together by a rookie in his lunch break. It's even called "The Experiment" since it was probably made as an experiment not as a playable "campaign".
The multiplayer, the game's primary focus, is bad as well, not like the single player mode but very close. There are a few nice ideas, like the zombies that start attacking you when you get hurt and your jammer gets disturbed, so you have to fend against both players as well as zombies when under fire. But the implementation of said ideas is lacking and the gameplay suffers a lot. Everything feels generic and ordinary. The controls are pretty bad. The most horrible thing is the mouse sensitivity that cannot be properly set across the whole game. You end up with lower sensitivity in menus and several orders of magnitude higher sensitivity within the gameplay. It might be a bug and not a general behavior but in my case it ruined the whole experience. Neither adjusting the sensitivity slider nor adjusting the mouse dpi helped too much as the issue remained there across the gameplay.
I'm glad I was able to test it during a free weekend. I was tempted to buy it several times before. Now I know for sure that in this state it's not worth buying it not even on sale.
TL;DR:
Don't buy it. It's bad. I played it during a free weekend and I already regret wasting my time on it.

Mark of the Ninja. Simply put it my favorite stealth game of all time. While in other stealth games I do resort to killing some, or all NPC's this game is different.
What is it that makes this game my favorite? The story, while simpel is really enjoyable and the graphic style of the game fits the story really well. The gameplay in it self is really good and you can play it with mouse and keyboard or with a controller, which ever you prefer.
Ubisoft tried to "copy" this game in their 2.5D Assasin's Creed Chronicle game, while they being ok if you really want a good stealth game there are few as good as Merk of the Ninja. (Maybe gunpoint, but that is mainly because I like Jazz music.) What comes to Mark of the Ninja's soundtrack it fits the game, but not memorable like Transistor or Bastion.
In the end, if you are looking for a really good stealth game this is your best bet. It can be forgiving if you are new to the whole genre and you can find a challenge in new game plus after compleating the game if you are looking for somthing more challeging.

holds up well after all these years but has some issues. It's definitely worth playing if you're interested, if you get it during a sale I highly doubt you'll be disappointed. It's the first game of the series, meaning that not everything is the best since they had no idea what would work well and what wouldn't, but damn if it isn't a good first game.
--------------
The story is fine, feels very Batman. The areas aren't very big by todays standard, but they are definitely well used and designed for going back through them multiple times. The progression feels natural, one thing leads to another without being extremely repetitive or awkward.
I found the sneaking & planning areas a lot of fun, big brawls feel satisfying when you pull off those combo moves and you honestly feel like Batman when you're sneaking around and the henchmen start freaking out because their friends are going down one by one with no sign of you.
The combat flows nicely once you get a hang of it but there are times when the controls feel a bit sluggish and you lose your combo because of a way too short time limit or from not going after the opponent the game expects you to. I've lost so many to the Weapon Specialists and stun batons when the game didn't go where I wanted it to. Also, it get's VERY repetitive with the "minibosses" that charge at you that felt more like a chore then anything else.
The voice acting is fantastic most of the time. With Mark Hamill as the Joker and Kevin Conroy as Batman it's hard to go wrong, but even the henchmen discussing their bad descisions didn't get repetitive as there seems to be a wide variety of lines based on location and time.
Boss Fights: Can be tricky to get right, requires concentration and strategy, but aren't difficult as long as you pay attention and time your skill wisely.
The riddles add a bit off deeper exploring as well as some easter eggs, but I didn't bother to go properly hunting for them and still ended up with 180 off them since I love to explore the nooks and crannies.
The AI is amazing for a game this old. They react to the enviroment, throw stuff, pick up discarded weapons and if you freak them out by picking them off one by one they start moving in groups for safety, shooting at weird sounds and checking for you a lot more thorougly.
As for the save system: A bit of a hassle, a wrong timed death can put you back quite a bit. You autosave when you enter/exit an area, as well as at certain stages of a boss fight. Can be annoying when picking up riddles because they reset if you die or exit the game at the wrong time. Has once or twice kicked me back a whole huge area or complex room because of an ill timed death.
Graphics are fine, doesn't look too dated with the atmospheric dark style even if some textures are a bit low res and non-combat animations can be a bit stiff. Ran smooth as butter on my dying GTX 680 and Windows 10.

A masterpiece amongst visual novels.
I've never been a fan of the horror genre, but Higurashi is an exception. Higurashi is different because it doesn't take "generic" horror cliches such as extreme amounts of gore or jump scares. If you've watched the anime or played the VN already, yes, I agree, it does take a while to get to the scary parts. But the build-up and the contrast makes it worth it. If you went into this game blind without even reading the description, you might even start to think it's just another romance visual novel. The lightheartedness of the beginning contrasting with the slowly ascending terror makes reading and continuing addicting.
I played the game with the voice patch installed. However, Higurashi is by origin a sound novel, where just the sounds alone are capable of giving you a great experience. But do yourself a favor and install that voice patch anyway. The voices help bring the characters to life, and it helps set the mood with the cute to evil switches.
If you've never experienced Higurashi When They Cry before, you're in for a ride. One playthrough won't be able to satisfy all the countless questions going through your head after the ending. Read it again and live in the world of Hinamizawa again, and try to figure out the mystery yourself and where things went wrong. Before you know it, you'll finish the game at 3 am, and not sleep until 11 am in fear of Rena waiting at your door.

If you like kinetic visual novels (that is, visual novels with just a story and no choices) I recommend you give this one a try.  Although there are several parts that have yet to be released for purchase, having just finished this one, I can confirm that it tells a complete story.  Engrossing and well worth the money.

Game Higurashi When They cry . ( ひぐらしのなく頃に )

*spoiler alert*
The characters and music are really charming, helping to get me into the story. The humor took quite an edge off the rather serious story, which is based on ethics and cultural differences--it touches on what's considered right vs wrong, good vs bad, emotion vs logic, what's considered precious, and other personal values that are important for getting along with others in society.
P.S. If it wasn't already implied somewhere, there's no real game play, just a story (~4-6 hours of reading) with hand drawn anime-style art and music to accompany it.
Most of this 1st installment was just an introduction to the characters and the setting, with the main characters being whisked away on an adventure in an extremely foreign land, and getting involved in some of the current drama.

Mark of the Ninja has great art, music, story, gameplay progression, stealth and cliffhanger.
It is essential for any stealth/moral (eg: Dishonred) fan or even just a fan of action games.
Mark Of The Ninja is a 2D Steath game with Puzzle elements and a progression system where you use points to chose perks in a progression tree such as more takedowns or more items.
There are costumes that you unlock as you progress through the game that change your playstyle
such as the path of wisdom that takes away your sword however grants you access to non-lethal takedowns.
The game features a unique shadows system where you will not be spotted when in the dark however some enemies have night vision and torches so they can spot you.
The graphics are visually stunning and looks more like a handrawn picture book than a game.

Definately a must-get for people who are into its genre. Different costumes that you can unlock suit different playstyles aswell as each room being completable in many different fashions. Will you slice through all your enemies, stealthily sneak around them, turn them against eachother, or even a mix of all or more? All in all, for the price, it's great to go in and try to 100%. It can be a bit frustrating if you're stuck at a bit but just try to be patient and carefully think it out. Occasionally, I would just try to rush through a room without thinking and it lead to rage-quits. Although the story isn't great, it's definately enough of to keep the player interested and is an insentive to get through.

I first played this on my office Mac Quadra years ago. This game's minimalist graphics and eerie soundtrack created incredible tension. Flashback was still a year or two out. Another World had that same tight gameplay and non-verbal storytelling with far less graphical technology behind it. It followed the same vien of Prince of Persia and Dark Castle where measuring spacebar jumps and timing spinning blades and falling rocks was the difference between life and starting the level over. Another World had me frustrated at first, but had me wanting to uncover the whole story. I've finished this game on three platforms so far...imagine my joy (and continued frustration) to find that it ended in a cliffhanger that would be resolved in a sequel.
Anyone who beats this game and doesn't immediately seek out the sequel title must have a heart of an alien.

A digital board game done right. This is what Gremlins Inc. is to me.
- Easy to learn but complicated enough to be fun for a lot of hours
- A huge amount of player interaction (fun interaction at that! Send your enemies to jail, swap places with them, take their money, do everything to stop their plans.)
- Very good art design.
- Superb audio
- Matchmaking system! Click a button and get to play with random strangers climbing the ladders or simply having fun.
From the negatives, i would say the game is somewhat RNG heavy and i generally dislike that. This game dropped the standard "roll the dice to move" mechanic and removed that part of rng which is good. There is however a lot of RNG involved in pretty much any spot on the map (roll the dice to get a misfortune, earn less money, go to jail).
All in all this is an excelent game i can highly reccomend to anyone looking for a "board game" to play with friends/strangers online.

A fun board game. Matches can take an hour or longer, but are not dull and basically anything can happen.
If you liked Munchkin, this game has the same sense of humour.
At the moment you need multiple copies to play with your friends, but the devs are looking into adding Hotseat support and there is even talk about adding local co-op by using Android/iOS devices.
If you're having physics problems, try turning on Vsync and that should fix it. High framerate can mess things up. Otherwise, good game.
